title: feat(wrappers): a copilot seat whose account may not use Copilot CLI (HTTP 403, "Access denied by policy settings") or whose Copilot policy blocks the moe MCP server stops once with one coded line instead of relaunch-looping
description:
Slice of task-59e1d150 (GitHub Copilot CLI as a fifth agent provider), found while settling that row's contract against the INSTALLED CLI. dependsOn task-49d4a565 (it adds the per-launch --log-dir and the post-run sign-out classification this row extends) and task-e266a150 (it edits the same parity files and owns the copilot guards gate). The closing row task-59e1d150 depends on this row.

MEASURED 2026-11-06 ~05:05Z by architect-a8e13516 on copilot 1.0.106 in WSL (Ubuntu-24.04, nvm node 24), signed in through `copilot login` with the human's GitHub account. Credit-free runs: each failed before any model turn.
1. NOT ENTITLED. A headless run with the slice argv (prompt on stdin, -C, --no-ask-user, --no-auto-update, --disable-builtin-mcps, --additional-mcp-config @file, --log-dir) exits 1. stderr: `Error: Access denied by policy settings (Request ID: <id>)`, then `Your Copilot CLI policy setting may be preventing access. This can happen when: ...` and `To resolve this, visit your Copilot settings: https://github.com/settings/copilot`. The run's own --log-dir file `process-<ts>-<pid>.log` holds `[ERROR] Error loading models: Error: 403 "unauthorized: not authorized to use this Copilot feature\n"`. task-49d4a565 classifies only `No authentication information found`, so this falls through to the generic launch-failure path, and under polling the wrapper relaunches with backoff forever.
2. MCP BLOCKED. In text mode copilot prints on stderr, before the model call: ` ! Third-party MCP servers are disabled by your organization's Copilot policy. Only built-in servers are available.` and ` ! 1 MCP server was blocked by policy: 'probe' (Could not verify server against any configured registry)`. The blocked server's process is never started. These lines are NOT in the process log, even at --log-level debug. With --output-format json they arrive as `session.warning` events (data.warningType `policy` and `mcp`). On an entitled account under such a policy, a seat would run without its moe and serena servers, so it can neither claim nor complete, and polling relaunches it.
3. For comparison, signed out (empty COPILOT_HOME, no token env): stderr `Error: No authentication information found.`, exit 1, and the log line `[ERROR] No authentication information found.` (task-49d4a565's case).

DELIVERABLE, in both wrappers with byte-identical strings, extending task-49d4a565's per-launch log dir and post-run classification (never a parallel path):
(a) After a NONZERO headless exit, the same scan of this launch's own log dir also matches `not authorized to use this Copilot feature`. It prints exactly one `[ERROR] MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED: ...` line. The line names the remedy: sign in with a GitHub account whose Copilot plan includes Copilot CLI (`copilot login`), or have the organization enable Copilot CLI (github.com/settings/copilot); Windows and WSL sign in separately; this seat exits instead of looping. Then one #general @governors escalation, heartbeat stop and exit 1, with no launch-failure backoff, as the sign-out route does.
(b) The headless launch keeps a private per-launch copy of copilot's stderr, still shown live. After ANY exit code, a line naming the moe server blocked (`MCP server was blocked by policy: 'moe'`) or `Third-party MCP servers are disabled` prints exactly one `[ERROR] MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED: ...` line, with the same escalation and stop. The remedy: an account or organization policy that allows MCP servers in Copilot (the moe and serena servers are local stdio servers, and no MCP registry allowlist may exclude them). A blocked `serena` alone prints one [WARN] and keeps the run's normal outcome. PowerShell must keep task-ab323f85's UTF-8 stdin pipe, the native exit code and its error preferences; under 5.1, stderr capture must not throw under Stop. The planner settles the mechanism (for example a 2>&1 pipeline that shows each stderr record live and appends it to the private file).
(c) Never echo whole logs or stderr copies, and never read a credential store. Clean the per-launch files on every exit path.

TESTS: extend task-ab323f85/49d4a565's recording fake and the postflight-vm-route.{sh,ps1} rows on bash, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7:
- a fake that writes the 403 log line and exits 1 (polling on, 1 s interval: exactly one launch);
- fakes that print the MCP-blocked stderr lines and exit 0 and exit 1;
- negatives: a blocked serena only; the phrases only on stdout; exit 0 with the 403 text in the log; a stale 403 log outside this launch's dir.

NOT IN SCOPE: docs (task-59e1d150 documents both codes), IDEs, any precheck that spends a model call. Parity: task-e266a150's MOE_COPILOT_ family compare covers the new codes automatically. Edit parity-check.{sh,ps1} only if e266a150 pins an exact MOE_COPILOT_ member list.

VERIFICATION: task-e266a150's gate shape (vm-route on bash/5.1/pwsh 7, ParseFile and bash -n, both parity checks, npm run lint), within 20 minutes; never the full postflight.
definitionOfDone: After a nonzero headless copilot exit whose own per-launch log holds `not authorized to use this Copilot feature`, moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 print exactly one MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED line with the remedy, send one #general escalation, stop the heartbeat and exit 1 after exactly one launch with polling on. An exit 0, an unrelated or missing log, or the phrase only in another launch's log never classify. postflight-vm-route rows pass on bash, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7.

When copilot's stderr for the launch reports the moe server blocked by policy (`MCP server was blocked by policy: 'moe'` or `Third-party MCP servers are disabled`), both wrappers print exactly one MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED line, escalate once and exit 1 without relaunching, whatever copilot's exit code. stderr is still shown live. A blocked serena alone prints one [WARN] and keeps the normal outcome, and the phrases only on stdout never classify. Same rows.

The private stderr copies and log dirs are per launch, cleaned on every exit path, and never echoed whole. PowerShell keeps the UTF-8 stdin pipe, the native exit code and its error preferences. Same rows.
checkRefs[0] passes within 20 minutes: vm-route on bash, 5.1 and pwsh 7, the wrapper parse checks, both parity checks and npm run lint. No full postflight, and no live package build.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.sh, in the copilot headless launch only: the TUI, 49d4a565's --help probe and every other CLI stay byte-identical. Read mem:gotcha-native-stderr-live-copy first (the measured bash and PowerShell patterns).
(a) Copy: COPILOT_ERR_FILE="$COPILOT_LOG_DIR.stderr" (use the landed log-dir variable): beside, never inside, the per-launch --log-dir 49d4a565 creates in the private secure temp dir, so copilot's log scan never reads it and the harness can find it. Create it empty with `: >` right after the log dir, in the same branch. Error handling: a failed creation takes 49d4a565's pre-launch route for a log dir that cannot be created (an explanatory error naming the path, exit 1, no launch); never launch without the copy.
(b) Run the landed command unchanged (argv, stdin file, Command: banner) but send only stderr through tee, with stdout still on the terminal: `{ (cd "${CLI_ROOT:-$PROJECT}" && agent_git_exec <landed argv> < "$COPILOT_PROMPT_FILE") 2>&1 1>&3 3>&- | tee -a "$COPILOT_ERR_FILE" >&2 3>&-; CLI_EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}; } 3>&1`, under the existing set +e. Read PIPESTATUS inside the group. Not `2> >(tee ...)`: its process substitution can still be writing when the scan reads the copy.
(c) Classification right after the run, where 49d4a565 checks the sign-in and before the generic launch-failure accounting. At most one coded line per launch, in this order:
1. 49d4a565's MOE_COPILOT_SIGNED_OUT check, unchanged.
2. CLI_EXIT_CODE != 0 and this launch's log dir holds `not authorized to use this Copilot feature` (49d4a565's scan: the same files, and a missing or unreadable log is no evidence): print `[ERROR] MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED: Copilot refused this GitHub account (HTTP 403): its Copilot plan or organization policy does not include Copilot CLI. Sign in with a GitHub account whose Copilot plan includes Copilot CLI (copilot login), or have the organization enable Copilot CLI (github.com/settings/copilot). Windows and WSL sign in separately; this seat exits instead of looping.` and escalate `@governors $WORKER_ID: MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED - Copilot refused the GitHub account of this seat (HTTP 403, no Copilot CLI access). Seat exiting and deregistering (the task returns to the queue); sign in with an account whose Copilot plan includes Copilot CLI, or have the organization enable it (github.com/settings/copilot), before relaunching.`
3. Any exit code, and `grep -qE "Third-party MCP servers are disabled|blocked by policy.*'moe'" "$COPILOT_ERR_FILE"` (one grep, no pipe; any line naming the moe server, so a plural 'servers were blocked' line counts too): print `[ERROR] MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED: the Copilot policy of this account blocked the moe MCP server, so this seat can neither claim nor complete a task. Use an account or organization whose Copilot policy allows MCP servers (github.com/settings/copilot); moe and serena are local stdio servers, and no MCP registry allowlist may exclude them. This seat exits instead of looping.` and escalate `@governors $WORKER_ID: MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED - the Copilot policy of this account blocked the moe MCP server, so the seat cannot claim or complete tasks. Seat exiting and deregistering (the task returns to the queue); allow MCP servers in the Copilot policy of the account or organization before relaunching.`
4. Else, a copy matching `grep -qE "blocked by policy.*'serena'"` prints one `[WARN] The Copilot policy of this account blocked the serena MCP server, so this run had no Serena tools (moe was not blocked). Allow MCP servers in the Copilot policy to restore them.` and the run keeps its normal outcome.
Each fatal route is the sign-out route: one #general escalation (transport errors swallowed, so a failed page never relaunches), remove this launch's log dir and copy, stop_heartbeat_sidecar, exit 1 (the EXIT trap deregisters and rescues any bytes), never the launch-failure backoff. If 49d4a565 wrote that tail inline, lift it into one small helper for the three codes, with SIGNED_OUT's text unchanged. Print the coded lines on the same stream as the landed SIGNED_OUT line. A missing or unreadable copy is no evidence; never print a log or the copy; never read a credential store.
(d) Remove "$COPILOT_LOG_DIR" and "$COPILOT_ERR_FILE" together wherever 49d4a565 removes the log dir; cleanup_temp's removal of the secure temp dir stays the fallback on every other exit, interruption included.
bash -n, then step 1's rows pass.
implementationPlan.note: moe-agent.sh copilot headless only. copilot_signed_out generalized to copilot_log_has DIR PHRASE (same files/skip rules; only caller). COPILOT_ERR_FILE="$COPILOT_LOG_DIR.stderr" created with `{ : > ..; } 2>/dev/null` right after the log dir; failure = '[ERROR] Cannot create private Copilot stderr copy <path>; refusing to launch.' exit 1, no launch. Run: `{ (...) 2>&1 1>&3 3>&- | tee -a COPY >&2 3>&-; CLI_EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]}; } 3>&1`. Classification SIGNED_OUT > NOT_ENTITLED (nonzero + own log) > MCP_BLOCKED (grep -qE copy, any exit) > serena [WARN]; log dir + copy removed together, then the landed copilot_fatal (stderr [ERROR] line, one #general @governors chat_send with errors swallowed, stop_heartbeat_sidecar, exit 1). Deviation from the plan text: the escalation content is copilot_fatal's landed shape ("@governors <worker>: <coded line>"), the same route SIGNED_OUT/ARGV_REJECTED use, not a second hand-written page text. bash -n OK; full postflight-vm-route.sh PASS (both [copilot] and [copilot policy] ok lines).

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1: the twin of step 2, in the copilot headless launch only, with byte-identical strings: both coded lines, the WARN, both escalations and both regexes.
(a) Copy: "$copilotLogDir.stderr" (the landed log-dir variable), beside the per-launch log dir 49d4a565 creates. Open it before the launch with `New-Object IO.StreamWriter($path, $true, (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))`. Error handling: a failure to open it takes 49d4a565's pre-launch route for the log dir (an explanatory error, $script:MoeExitStatus = 1, exit 1, no launch).
(b) Run, per mem:gotcha-native-stderr-live-copy (probed on 5.1.26100 and 7.6.9). Keep ab323f85's UTF-8 switch of $global:OutputEncoding and [Console]::OutputEncoding (mem:gotcha-ps1-native-stdin-utf8). Save $ErrorActionPreference and set 'Continue': under Stop, 5.1 throws NativeCommandError on the first redirected stderr record. Then `& { $body | Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand <landed argv>; $script:CliExitCode = $LASTEXITCODE } 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { if ($_ -is [Management.Automation.ErrorRecord]) { $line = $_.Exception.Message; [Console]::Error.WriteLine($line); try { $writer.WriteLine($line) } catch {} } else { $_ | Out-Host } }`. In finally, dispose the writer and restore the error preference and both encodings. Use $_.Exception.Message, never "$_": 5.1 turns a blank stderr line into the text System.Management.Automation.RemoteException. A throw inside ForEach-Object would stop copilot, so no write may throw out of it. The piped body keeps Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand's ExpectingInput stdin route (probed).
(c) After the run, step 2's order. SIGNED_OUT stays unchanged. A nonzero exit plus the log phrase gives MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED. The copy, read as UTF-8 (missing or unreadable = no evidence), matching -cmatch "Third-party MCP servers are disabled|blocked by policy.*'moe'" gives MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED. Otherwise -cmatch "blocked by policy.*'serena'" gives the WARN (yellow, as other warnings). -cmatch keeps grep's case-sensitivity, and .NET's . never crosses a line break, so whole-text matching equals the sh per-line grep. The fatal route is the sign-out route: Invoke-MoeRpc chat_send to $generalChannelId in try/catch, remove both per-launch paths, Stop-HeartbeatSidecar, $script:MoeExitStatus = 1, exit 1. Use the shared helper if step 2 lifted one.
(d) Remove the copy wherever the log dir is removed, the outer-finally fallback included.
Run ParseFile on 5.1 and 7. Step 3's rows pass, and ab323f85's CP-H (U+2014 on stdin) still passes on 5.1, which proves the stdin pipe.

- the same on pwsh 7;
- bash: bash -n, vm-route, parity-check.sh and npm run lint.
Green needs 3 PASS_GATE, 3 'PASS postflight-vm-route' and 3 '[copilot policy] ok ' lines. Every Windows hop goes through /init (mem:gotcha-wsl-interop-binfmt-init).

- A polling row that hangs to the 360 s timeout is a missed classification.
- If the whole gate passes 1200 s on an idle host, report it with the leg times instead of dropping rows or assertions.
Never run npm install, a build or package tests in the shared checkout, and never the full postflight.{sh,ps1} (mem:decision-mid-epic-launcher-gate-narrow). Signal only PIDs you started.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A headless copilot seat whose GitHub account may not use Copilot CLI (HTTP 403 in this launch's own --log-dir after a nonzero exit), or whose Copilot policy blocks the moe MCP server (copilot's stderr for this launch, at any exit code), stops once with exactly one coded line, one #general escalation and exit 1, instead of relaunch-looping. A serena-only block prints one [WARN] and keeps the run's normal outcome. stderr is still shown live, through a private per-launch copy that is cleaned on every exit path.
acceptanceCriteria: After a nonzero headless copilot exit whose own per-launch log holds `not authorized to use this Copilot feature`, moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 print exactly one MOE_COPILOT_NOT_ENTITLED line with the remedy, send one #general escalation, stop the heartbeat and exit 1 after exactly one launch with polling on. An exit 0, an unrelated or missing log, or the phrase only in another launch's log never classify. postflight-vm-route rows pass on bash, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7.

When copilot's stderr for the launch reports the moe server blocked by policy (`MCP server was blocked by policy: 'moe'` or `Third-party MCP servers are disabled`), both wrappers print exactly one MOE_COPILOT_MCP_BLOCKED line, escalate once and exit 1 without relaunching, whatever copilot's exit code. stderr is still shown live. A blocked serena alone prints one [WARN] and keeps the normal outcome, and the phrases only on stdout never classify. Same rows.

The private stderr copies and log dirs are per launch, cleaned on every exit path, and never echoed whole. PowerShell keeps the UTF-8 stdin pipe, the native exit code and its error preferences. Same rows.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Scanning copilot's --log-dir for the MCP policy lines: rejected. Measured: they never reach the process log, even at --log-level debug.
- --output-format json and parsing session.warning events: rejected. It changes the headless transcript operators read and the stdout contract ab323f85/49d4a565 test; text-mode stderr carries the same lines.
- bash `2> >(tee ...)`: rejected. The process substitution is asynchronous, so the scan could read a partial copy. The brace-group pipeline with fd 3 is synchronous and keeps stdout on the terminal (probed).
- PowerShell .NET Process with RedirectStandardError: rejected. It bypasses Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand (git guard env, .cmd resolution, ExpectingInput stdin). 2>&1 | ForEach-Object is the shape the ps1 claude headless launch already uses.
- PowerShell flags set in-stream with no file: smaller, but the deliverable names a private per-launch copy and DoD 3 checks it, so ps1 keeps a file like sh.
- An entitlement or policy precheck before the run: out of scope (it spends a model call or reads credentials).
- Matching only the exact `MCP server was blocked by policy: 'moe'`: widened to a line with `blocked by policy` then `'moe'`, which also covers a plural `servers were blocked` line; a serena-only line still only warns.
- Precedence SIGNED_OUT > NOT_ENTITLED > MCP_BLOCKED: each later fix only matters once the earlier one is done, and the MCP policy is per account, so an account change comes first. One coded line and one escalation per launch.
- Parity edits: none. e266a150's MOE_COPILOT_ family compare covers both new codes; the serena WARN has no code and the twin rows pin its text.

- agent_git_exec is a subshell function that execs the CLI; moe-agent.sh has no global pipefail.

planningNotes.risks:
- The prerequisites are unlanded: every ab323f85/49d4a565 symbol named here is a planning expectation. Read the landed diffs first and adapt; never duplicate.
- Gate time: 651 s at load ~10 before the prerequisites' rows and these; the budget is 1200 s. Keep each new row to one wrapper run.
- An MCP server or descendant that outlives copilot keeps the stderr pipe open and the wrapper waits. The claude headless 2>&1 launch has the same exposure.
- An MCP-blocked run may still have edited files. The fatal exit leaves them to the existing EXIT-trap / outer-finally rescue, as SIGNED_OUT does; it adds no new landing route.
- 5.1 traps: NativeCommandError under Stop, the RemoteException text for a blank stderr line, OEM decoding of captured stdout, a throw inside ForEach-Object stopping copilot.
- The sh [ERROR]/[WARN] tags carry ANSI colour: assert the text after the tag.
